description:
The Sruthitharangam scheme is a significant initiative launched by the Government of Kerala in India to provide cochlear implants to children with hearing impairments. 

The scheme was officially launched on 12th December 2019. 

It aims to enhance the quality of life for children suffering from profound hearing loss. 

The primary objective of the Sruthitharangam scheme is to provide financial assistance for cochlear implantation. 

The scheme targets children aged between 0 to 18 years. 

It specifically focuses on those who are diagnosed with profound hearing loss. 

The scheme aims to provide a total of 1,000 cochlear implants over a period of five years. 

This translates to an average of 200 cochlear implants being provided each year. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is substantial. 

Each cochlear implant costs approximately INR 6 lakh. 

The Kerala government covers the entire cost of the cochlear implant surgery and rehabilitation. 

This includes pre-operative assessments, the surgical procedure, and post-operative rehabilitation. 

The scheme also provides for the necessary audiological and speech therapy sessions. 

These sessions are crucial for the effective use of the cochlear implant. 

The eligibility criteria for the Sruthitharangam scheme are clearly defined. 

Children must be residents of Kerala to qualify for the scheme. 

They must also be diagnosed with profound hearing loss by a recognized medical professional. 

The income limit for families to be eligible for the scheme is set at INR 3 lakh per annum. 

This income criterion ensures that the benefits reach economically weaker sections of society. 

Parents or guardians must provide proof of income while applying for the scheme. 

The application process for the Sruthitharangam scheme is straightforward. 

Interested families must fill out the application form available at designated government hospitals. 

They must submit the application along with required documents. 

These documents include the child's birth certificate, income certificate, and medical reports. 

The medical reports must confirm the diagnosis of profound hearing loss. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by a committee of medical professionals. 

The committee assesses the eligibility and medical necessity for the cochlear implant. 

If approved, the family is notified about the next steps in the process. 

The surgery is typically conducted at government hospitals or empaneled private hospitals. 

The timeline for the entire process from application to surgery can vary. 

However, families can expect the surgery to be scheduled within a few months of approval. 

Post-surgery, the child will require regular follow-ups and therapy sessions. 

These sessions are essential for the child to adapt to the cochlear implant. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of family involvement in the rehabilitation process. 

Families are encouraged to participate in therapy sessions to support their child's development. 

The implementing authority for the Sruthitharangam scheme is the Kerala State Government. 

Specifically, the Department of Health and Family Welfare oversees the scheme. 

For any inquiries or assistance, families can contact the Department of Health and Family Welfare. 

The contact details for the department can be found on the official Kerala government website. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from families who have benefited from it. 

Many parents have reported significant improvements in their children's communication skills. 

The cochlear implants have allowed children to integrate better into society. 

They have also improved their educational opportunities. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Kerala government to promote inclusivity. 

It aligns with the government's commitment to enhancing the quality of life for all citizens. 

The Sruthitharangam scheme also reflects the government's focus on healthcare accessibility. 

By providing cochlear implants free of cost, the government aims to reduce the financial burden on families. 

The scheme has been instrumental in raising awareness about hearing impairments. 

It has encouraged early diagnosis and intervention for children with hearing loss. 

The success of the scheme is measured by the number of cochlear implants provided each year. 

As of 2023, the scheme has successfully provided over 500 cochlear implants since its inception. 

This indicates a strong uptake of the program among eligible families. 

The government continues to promote the scheme through various outreach programs. 

These programs aim to educate families about the benefits of cochlear implants. 

The Sruthitharangam scheme is a vital step towards ensuring that children with hearing impairments receive the support they need. 

It not only addresses medical needs but also fosters social inclusion and educational advancement. 

Overall, the scheme represents a significant investment in the future of children with hearing loss in Kerala. 

The commitment of the Kerala government to this cause is commendable. 

It sets a precedent for other states to consider similar initiatives. 

In conclusion, the Sruthitharangam scheme is a comprehensive program designed to assist children with profound hearing loss. 

It provides financial support for cochlear implants and emphasizes the importance of rehabilitation. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's dedication to improving healthcare access for all citizens. 

Families interested in the scheme should gather the necessary documents and apply promptly. 

This initiative has the potential to change lives and empower children with hearing impairments. 

The future of the Sruthitharangam scheme looks promising as it continues to evolve and expand its reach.
